methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort with landmark analysis design to mitigate immortal time bias. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression appropriately applied. Stratified analysis by treatment timing. Well-designed approach to addressing temporal confounding in observational data.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort demonstrating association between early hormonal therapy initiation and improved OS in synchronous bone-metastatic HSPC. Direct clinical relevance to treatment sequencing decisions in metastatic prostate cancer.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-aligned reporting with clear methodology and statistical approach. However, limited detail on data completeness and no explicit data availability statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Treatment timing in metastatic prostate cancer previously studied; study extends existing knowledge with landmark analysis approach. Meaningful but incremental contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Adequate organization and clarity. Some sections could be more concise.

key_strengths: Landmark analysis design appropriately addresses immortal time bias in assessing treatment timing effects
Single-center data extraction reduces heterogeneity in treatment protocols
Clear association between early initiation of novel hormonal therapy and OS improvement
key_concerns: Single-center China cohort limits generalizability; no external validation
Limited discussion of potential confounders in treatment selection
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective study with appropriate landmark analysis addressing temporal bias. Suitable for tier 3 with minor revisions and external validation needed.
